newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kinkel calls on Bosnians to join forces.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel calls on Bosnians to join forces.

text.p: Germany's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel appealed on Monday to Bosnia's communities to join forces and rebuild their country now that the results of its first post-war elections had been certified.
In a foreign ministry statement, Kinkel said confirmation of the results paved the way for creating democratic structures.

"The path is now free for the creation of democratic structures. On the basis of the election results joint institutions, envisaged in the Dayton peace accord, should be set up without delay," he said.
"I appeal to all three ethnic groups to accept responsibility for their country by constructively cooperating with each other," Kinkel was quoted as saying in the statement.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the international body supervising Bosnia's first post-war elections, announced on Sunday it had certified the results of national balloting on September 14.

The OSCE decision ended days of haggling over voting irregularities, although many critics of the Dayton peace process still say it is likely to lead to de facto partition of Bosnia between Croats, Serbs and Moslems.
